name: AI Research
guide:
AI Research roles center on pushing what a model can actually do, not on shipping it into a product. A research scientist or research engineer in this discipline runs experiments, tests new architectures or training recipes, and writes up results, sometimes for internal use and sometimes as a published paper or technical report. This is different from Machine Learning Engineering, which focuses on taking a model that already works and making it fast, reliable, and deployable at scale in production systems. It also differs from AI Safety and Alignment, which asks whether a model behaves the way it should and builds the guardrails, evaluations, and red teaming that catch when it does not. Someone in AI Research is usually asking whether the model can be made better, while ML Engineering asks whether it can be made to run, and Safety and Alignment asks whether it can be trusted.

A PhD genuinely matters for roles that require inventing new methods, publishing at top venues, or leading a research agenda, especially at labs like Anthropic and OpenAI where research scientist postings often assume that background. For research engineer roles, a strong publication record or a visible open-source contribution, a widely used library, a benchmark submission, a well-documented reproduction of a hard paper, can substitute for the degree entirely. There are no widely recognized certifications specific to AI research, and the postings in our data do not ask for one, so we will not invent one here. What employers actually screen for is evidence a candidate can do the work, meaning code, papers, or results that others can check. A master's degree paired with demonstrated research output is a common and viable path into this field.

Early career entry usually comes through an internship or a first research engineer role, and our data shows seven internship postings in this category right now, mostly labeled Research Engineer Intern. From there, the mid-level tier is where most of the market sits. Of the postings we pulled, 157 carry a Mid-level seniority tag, and this is where someone with a few years of hands-on model training and a track record of shipped experiments competes. Senior, Staff, and Principal titles account for the next tier up, roughly 58 postings combined, and these roles expect a body of work behind them, published papers, benchmarks the person has moved, or infrastructure other researchers now rely on. What actually gets someone hired at any level is verifiable output rather than years alone, a paper accepted somewhere real, a strong benchmark result, or an open-source repository other researchers cite or build on.

The skills most frequently listed across these postings are Large Language Models, appearing 116 times, and Reinforcement Learning, appearing 95 times, which together describe most of where research effort in the field is currently pointed. Python remains the baseline language, showing up in 98 postings, and PyTorch is the dominant deep learning framework with 71 mentions, while JAX appears in 31 postings, common at labs doing large-scale training research. Rust shows up often too, in 112 postings, reflecting a push toward faster and more reliable research infrastructure rather than just prototyping code. Beyond the core stack, postings call for distributed systems experience, fine-tuning work, model evaluation, Kubernetes, and CUDA, along with AWS as the leading cloud platform at 98 mentions. Model evaluation skills appear in 41 postings, a reminder that much of the job is measuring whether an idea actually worked, not just trying it.

Based on what we currently track, we see approximately 166 open AI Research postings live today, out of 230 total postings gathered in our recent pull. Salary data is thin in this category. Only 15 of those 230 postings, about 7 percent, list both a minimum and maximum salary figure, and among that small group the range runs from 75,788 dollars to 249,272 dollars per year, with an average minimum near 138,826 dollars and an average maximum near 160,744 dollars. Because so few postings disclose pay, treat that range as a narrow sample rather than a market-wide figure. Anthropic is the company posting most often in this category with 43 listings, followed by Scale AI with 21 and OpenAI with 18, with Waymo, ServiceNow, and Databricks rounding out the next tier of frequent hirers.
